topic: Someone discovers their neighbor is secretly wealthy
text: I can scarce believe it, how Simon, he who’s always got a hand out in the market, turns out to have gold as deep as a summer’s wheat field. Mind you, I’ve always known that man’s got a knack for the earth, could coax a bloom from the meanest of clods. But gold? That’s a rare sight in these parts. I can’t help but think back to the times when I borrowed a plow, or a sheaf, or even a bit of seed, and he’d act so stricken, like he didn’t have a coin to his name. Now, I hear tell he’s got more than the miller himself. It’s a strange world, where the meek shall inherit the earth, or so they say. But it makes one wonder what truly lies beneath the soil we toil day in and day out.
